newsitem.title: BRAZIL: U.S. advisor sees higher exports to LatAm region.
newsitem.headline: U.S. advisor sees higher exports to LatAm region.

text.p: U.S. exports to Latin American and Caribbean countries will exceed $100 billion this year and are expected to reach $240 billion by 2010, said Thomas McLarty, U.S. President Bill Clinton's advisor for Latin America.

McLarty, who spoke at a luncheon at the Business Future of the Americas Forum, praised the bilateral relationship established with Brazil in particular, which he expects to improve as the Brazilian economy keeps stabilizing.
"Our relationship with Brazil has never been better," said McLarty, adding that the economic reforms introduced by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso "have truly transformed the country."
U.S. exports to Brazil increased 40 percent in 1995, while U.S. investment in the country totaled $5.4 billion between January and August, 200 percent over the same period last year.
He expects U.S. investment in Brazil to reach $7.0 billion by year's end.
